reason: Both conversations over-escalate on a single faint smell weeks ago (ground truth says no critical safety stop was warranted), so neither reached the carbon-brush inspection. Conversation 1 followed the expected sensible first step (unplug, turn the drum by hand) with careful safety wording and made no unsupported claims. Conversation 2 led with 'most likely a broken belt' before any evidence, then after the belt proved intact invented a confident 'thermal fuse / motor' diagnosis that is unsupported and almost certainly wrong given the hidden truth of worn brushes, steering the owner toward an expensive engineer call for a £10-£20 DIY fix. Conversation 1's honesty and absence of fabricated diagnosis make it the better service despite its premature stop.
